cold_open.hook: Nvidia down 2%, AMD down nearly 8%—but one of them just announced it's literally paying people to use its software

markets.macro_note: Tech weakness dragging broad indices; defensive plays and energy holding up

big_story.story_title: Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) Announces a Profit-Sharing Program For Its Computing Framework Access
big_story.angle: Nvidia is so desperate to lock in developers that it's literally cutting them a check—a sign the AI infrastructure arms race is shifting from 'build it' to 'beg people to use it.'

quick_hits.angle: Microsoft's Xbox spinoff plan is basically admitting that owning a gaming studio is now a liability, not an asset—the hardware maker wants out of the creativity business.
Nigel Farage quits Parliament mid-scandal to fight a special election—the political equivalent of rage-quitting a video game to reset your save file.
Obamacare enrollment is plummeting in key states—not because people don't want coverage, but because the messaging has gone silent and confusion is winning.
Trump signals openness to selling F-35s to Turkey—a NATO ally that's also been cozying up to Russia, so basically we're selling advanced fighter jets to a country that might show them to Moscow.

odd_thing.joke_angle: iRobot's newest floor cleaner isn't a robot—it's a Roomba that gave up and decided to just be a really expensive broom with an app.
